findings.detail: needs an LSI index and has none — run `bun run lsi index --instance agent-skills --graph library`

not evaluated: `actor-roles-resolve` is `repo`-scoped and this run is scoped to agent-skills. An actor is declared ONCE at the repository root (`.claude/skills/actors/`) while a role is a swimlane inside one instance's diagrams, so this compares a repository-level set against an instance-level one. MEASURED 2026-09-26: `--instance ./bootstrap` produced 73 findings, one for almost every one of the 36 repository actors, because they name roles the bootstrap graph does not declare. Every one was false.

not evaluated: `actor-capabilities-resolve` is `repo`-scoped and this run is scoped to agent-skills. Both sides are repository-level — actors and `.claude/skills/capabilities/` are resolved through `repoRootFor`, so `--instance` does not move either. Re-asking per instance would re-derive the root's own answer once per declaration and report the same findings N times.

not evaluated: `actor-permissions-resolve` is `repo`-scoped and this run is scoped to agent-skills. Same shape as `actor-capabilities-resolve`: actors and `skills/permissions/permissions.json` are both repository-level, so an instance run can only duplicate the root's verdict.

not evaluated: `actor-is-not-a-role` is `repo`-scoped and this run is scoped to agent-skills. The subject set is `ACTOR_DIR`, resolved through `repoRootFor`, so it is repository-level and `--instance` does not move it. An instance run would re-derive the root's verdict over the same actor files and report the same findings once per declaration.

not evaluated: `nested-instance-audited` is `repo`-scoped and this run is scoped to agent-skills. `unreadNestedInstances()` walks from `repoRootFor(root)` to find declarations, so it asks a question ABOUT the repository's set of instances. MEASURED 2026-09-26: it fired 15 inside the bootstrap run, reporting bootstrap's siblings as unread from inside bootstrap — which is the root's question being asked in a place that cannot act on it.
